page: Microsoft Azure F8als_v6 is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Falsv6 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC 9V74 cores running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable. The hypervisor layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing and text generation for small LLM models also demonstrate strong performance. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, falls within the average range. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth, where read-only large block operations are weak, placing in the bottom 25%, while small block cached reads and large block writes remain average.

Given its compute-focused hardware profile with dedicated AMD EPYC cores and a lower memory allocation, this instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, text processing, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference. However, its lack of local storage and lower memory-to-core ratio make it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing.
